minutes_text:
Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES November 4, 2021

A meeting of the Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission was convened on November 4, 2021
via Zoom. Chairman Denmon called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.
Roll Call
Present
  Commissioner Lee Denmon, District One
  Commissioner Jacob Fragoso, District Two
  Commissioner Cynthia McLemore, District Three
  Commissioner Christopher Beck, District Four
  Sabrina Barnes, Director - Parks, Recreation and Community Services
  Teresa Estrada, Recreation Superintendent
  Juan Mata, Parks Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia, Food Services Manager
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
Absent
  Commissioner Henry Brown, Commissioner at Large
Public Comments

  None
Approval of the Minutes
  Commissioner McLemore made a motion to approve the minutes from October 7, 2021.
Commissioner Denmon seconded and the minutes were approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore and Denmon
  Nays: None

Staff Report
  Staff presented a staff report recommending the Parks and Recreation Commission
recommend the Mayor and Council Members approve Amendment Eight of the Elderly Nutrition
Program Services Subaward Number ENP202101 (City Agreement No. 20-201) with County of Los
Angeles Workforce Development Aging and Community Services (WDACS) to extend the period of
performance for CARES Act Funding in the amount of $108,542.00 to June 30, 2022. (Grant Funds)
  Commissioner Fragoso made a motion to approve the staff report and Commissioner
McLemore seconded. The motion was approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore and Denmon
  Nays: None

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES November 4, 2021

  Staff presented a staff report recommending the Parks and Recreation Commission
recommend the Mayor and Council Members take the following actions:
  a. Award the Vincent Park Restroom Project Phase 1 Project (CB-21-12) to PUB
  Construction, Inc.: and,
  b. Approve an agreement with PUB Construction, Inc. in an amount not to exceed,
  $545,000, including a contingency amount of $54,500, for a total cost of $599,500
  per Bid No. CB-21-12 (CDBG and General Fund)

  Commissioner Denmon asked how staff determined awarding PUB Construction, Inc.
Director Barnes stated a bid was issued and eight (8) vendors responded. The initial lowest vendor
was non-responsive. Staff moved onto to PUB Construction, Inc. who was the second lowest bidder.
  Commissioner Fragoso made a motion to approve the staff report. Commissioner Denmon
seconded and the motion was approved as follows:
  Ayes: Commissioners Fragoso, McLemore and Denmon
  Nays: None

Verbal Reports

  Juan Mata gave a verbal report on behalf of the Parks Administration regarding the following:
    The Graffiti Crew removed a tremendous amount of graffiti in Districts 2 and 4.
    At last month’s meeting there was a question about the graffiti located at the rooftop of 317
  S. La Brea Avenue. The owners have since removed the graffiti.

  Commissioner McLemore thanked staff and stated she drove by and the property looks
much better.

  Commissioner Denmon asked for status on the removal of the graffiti at Darby Park.

  Teresa Estrada gave a verbal report on behalf of the Recreation Division regarding the
following:
   Annual Holiday Turkey Giveaway: The City of Inglewood will host its 7th Annual Turkey
  Giveaway Presented by Pepsi, on Tuesday, November 23rd, from 9 a.m. to 12 p.m. with
  Snoop Dogg, on the grounds of Hollywood Park. This Drive-Thru only event will serve 2,500
  Inglewood residents, providing turkeys donated by Don Lee Farms, a bag of sides and
  additional items from Pepsi. No walk-ups will be taken and pre-registration required.
   Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony: The City’s annual Holiday Tree Lighting Ceremony will
  take place on Monday, November 29, at 6:30 p.m. at the Fabulous Forum. There will be live
  entertainment, refreshments, stockings for the kids and a special appearance from Santa
  himself.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES November 4, 2021

    Health Education: Join us each month as we share and collaborate on the many aspects of
  living a healthier lifestyle. Classes will provide education, insight, and resources that will
  assist in improving health today and empower individuals to continue to make healthier
  decisions tomorrow. All classes are FREE!
   Location: Darby Park – 3400 W. Arbor Vitae, Inglewood, CA 90305
   Time: 10:00 a.m. – 11:00 a.m.
   Topics:
  a. November 13, 2021 Understanding Diabetes: Methods to Minimize Your
  Risks and Tips to Manage Your Diagnosis.
  b. December 11, 2021, 10 Warning Signs of Alzheimer’s disease
  c. January 8, 2022 Medication Management in the Home February 12, 2022
  Understanding & Managing Hypertension and Other Cardiac Diseases.
  Register online at parksrec.cityofinglewood.org. For additional information, please call (310)
  412-8750.
    Family Paint Days: The Department is excited to offer Family Paint Days for the community.
  Workshops will give families the opportunity to make their own creative art to take home. All
  materials are provided. Instructors provide step-by-step painting instructions and everyone
  produces the same piece of art. On Saturday, November 13, 2021, from 11:30 a. m. to 1:30
  p.m. we will be at Darby Park - 3400 W. Arbor Vitae, Inglewood, CA 90305. On Saturday,
  December 11, 2021 11:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m. we will be at Rogers Park - 400 W. Beach
  Avenue, Inglewood, CA 90302. Finally, on Saturday, January 15, 2021 11:30 a.m. to 1:30
  p. m. we will be at the Veteran’s Memorial Building - 330 Centinela Avenue, Inglewood, CA
  90302
  Cost is $15 per person ages 5+. Register online at parksrec.cityofinglewood.org. For
  additional information, please call (310) 412-8750.

  Bharat Devlia gave a verbal report on behalf of the Human Services Division regarding the
following:
   Nutrition: Our Elderly Nutrition Program continues to deliver seven (7) meals per week to
  seniors ages 60 and over, along with weekly fresh produce deliveries, collaborating with the
  Social Justice Learning Institute, and provide monthly shelf stable meal packages in
  collaboration with the Los Angeles Food Bank.
   Child & Adult Care Food Program (CACFP): Offered at three sites:
   Rogers Park
   Darby Park
   Crenshaw Library
  The program remains GRAB-N-GO for youth ages 18 years and younger. Parents may pick
  meals up without the children being present.
   Our senior and disable Transportation Program continues to provide senior trips to critical
  appointments such as dialysis, and doctor’s appointments. Drivers and passengers continue
  to wear face mask and practice safe social distancing during transport. We are also
  scheduling drivers to transport seniors and disabled persons to other requested
  3
   Park and Recreation Commission
  MINUTES November 4, 2021

  appointments. We continue to assist with transporting Inglewood police officers to and from
  SoFi Stadium for events. We have also been transporting minimal number of participants
  who are attending the limited classes at the Senior Center since its soft opening.
    The Senior Center is hosting a COVID booster shot clinic on Wednesday, November 10th
  from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. Seniors can call to schedule appointments anytime.
    The Senior Center is also hosting emergency preparedness trainings and provides a
  meeting place to discuss both Measure H and I for the community.

Public Comments

  None

Commissioners Comments

  Commissioner McLemore thanked staff for their reports.

  Commissioner Denmon reminded everyone of the time change set for the upcoming
weekend.

  Commissioner Beck apologized to the Commission and staff for being late.

With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:22 p.m.
